uma.d: An architecture in which CPU and GPU share the same physical memory (on the GB10, ~121.7 GiB of visible LPDDR5X). Everything vLLM reserves comes out of the operating system, the page cache and the other processes.

fp8-ds-mla.d: Packed KV layout for sparse MLA: per token and layer, 512 B of FP8 latent + 16 B of scales + 128 B of BF16 RoPE = 656 B. In GLM-5.3-Flash (NoPE), the 128 B of RoPE are padding zeros. This is the layout of the V3.2/GLM geometry (576); in DeepSeek-V4 the same name refers to a 584 B row (448 FP8 + 128 B of BF16 RoPE + 8 B of UE8M0 scales), byte-for-byte identical to nvfp4_ds_mla.

headless.d: A vLLM rank that only executes the model, with no API server (--headless). In the GLM recipe, the worker (rank 1) runs this way; the API and the scheduler live on the head.

ssh-batchmode.d: ssh -o BatchMode=yes: it never asks for a password or confirmation; if the key doesn't authenticate, it fails immediately. This is what lets a launcher control the remote node without hanging on a prompt.

flock.d: A cooperative Linux lock on a file (flock -n fails if there is already an owner; flock -w N waits N s). It serializes start/restart/stop so that two launchers don't destroy each other.

fail-fast.d: Failing as early as possible, before causing damage: validating the configuration before stopping the healthy pair, or aborting the wait for /health when a rank has already died.

overlay-runtime.d: A patch script mounted into the container and applied on every start, before vllm serve, on top of the installed vLLM code. It changes without an image rebuild; it requires a fixed order and idempotency.

entrypoint.d: The command a container runs when it comes up. The recipe replaces the image's with --entrypoint bash IMAGE /start.sh: a script generated by the launcher that applies the overlays and runs exec vllm serve.

speculative-config.d: vLLM's JSON that configures speculative decoding: method (dflash, mtp…), drafter model, number of speculated tokens, drafter KV dtype, drafter TP, and the sampling and rejection methods.

canario-boot.d: A minimal sanity test after /health: “Reply with OK.” at temperature 0 and a draft acceptance > 0. It catches degenerate engines that keep answering 200.

contrato-log.d: A log-line format with fixed keys and a version (schema), read by verification tools. Changing the format requires bumping the version, just like an API.

pin-binario.d: Pinning the SHA-256 of a compiled artifact (e.g., cooperative_moe.so) and refusing any other. A rebuild with a different toolchain changes the hash and forces you to requalify the numerics.

perfil-servico.d: A coherent set of knobs for one kind of use (maximum context, long coding sessions, 3-node throughput…). The values are tuned together: seqs, MNBT, capture sizes and KV pool.

mnbt.d: Abbreviation the recipes use for --max-num-batched-tokens: the token budget of one scheduler step, adding up decodes (with drafts) and prefill chunks. In the GLM recipe it's also the size of the vision encoder cache (7168).

fat-expert.d: An expert that, in one step, receives more rows (tokens) than EXL3_TEMP_ROWS_FUSED and therefore leaves the fused exl3_moe. In a 7168-token prefill chunk the average is 7168 × 8 / 288 ≈ 199 rows per expert, so almost all of them are fat; E2 (EXL3_FAT_KERNEL) and E3 (EXL3_FAT_GROUPED) are the kernel tiers that process them, E3 in 3 launches per layer.

id-de-bloco.d: The allocation unit of the BlockPool shared by all KV groups. In GLM TP2, 1 ID = one 3584-token page across the 11 MLA layers + the 11 indexer ones = 27,163,136 B (~25.9 MiB); Mamba states and drafter blocks also take whole IDs, which is why capacity is counted in IDs, not bytes.

gate-memoria-boot.d: vLLM's startup check that refuses to come up if free memory is below gpu_memory_utilization × total (on UMA, read from MemAvailable). With --kv-cache-memory-bytes, this is the only role left for util: it no longer sizes the KV.

restricao-de-motor.d: A constraint born from fitting the model into the pieces of a specific inference engine, not from the hardware or the model. It disappears when the engine changes. In the GLM recipe on vLLM, the 512→576 KV pad and the 3,584-token pages are examples; on TensorFold v1.3.2, the limits of 2 ranks and 4 requests, which v1.4 and v1.5 lifted: engine constraints move when the engine moves.

paridade-conferida.d: A startup check in which the ranks all-gather a vector with the settings that change collectives or drafts and refuse to start if it differs (on TensorFold, before loading the weights). It complements parity by construction (the same script and the same environment on both ranks), which on its own only reveals a divergence when NCCL hangs.
